import copy
import time

class View:
    def __init__(self):
        self.rows = []
        self.notes = {}
        self.loading = False
        self.error = None
        self.seq = 0
        # Track the latest valid request id, and whether it has been finished
        self._current_request_id = None
        self._finished_request_ids = set()
    
    def begin(self, query):
        # Clear loading errors but keep existing rows until a valid finish
        self.error = None  # Clears any previous error
        # Start a new request with monotonically increasing id
        self.seq += 1
        current_id = self.seq
        # Make this the "latest" active request
        self._current_request_id = current_id
        return current_id
    
    def finish(self, request_id, rows):
        # Only the latest begun request can update rows, once.
        # Check: is this request_id == our current/latest pending request?
        if request_id != self._current_request_id:
            # Stale/old/duplicate/idle return False and do not affect state (rows same as before unless we want to keep existing)  
            return False
        
        # Also, a request id that was already finished should not be accepted again.
        if request_id in self._finished_request_ids:
            return False
        
        # Mark this request complete
        self._current_request_id = None
        self._finished_request_ids.add(request_id)
        
        # Accept/replace rows
        self.rows = copy.deepcopy(rows)
        return True
